description: Golden cases for the two hashes a v2 ownership marker carries. A kwargs case gives JSON text, the canonical text it encodes to and the hash of that text, or an error the failure must name. A body case gives a body and its hash. Hashes are sha256: followed by 64 lower-case hex digits. The expected values were computed by an independent Python implementation of the rules, not by Sedum.

cases.why: One of three spellings of the integer 1. A writer that keeps the spelling of a number hashes the same value to different hashes. Integer-valued numbers have one canonical text whatever they were written as.

One of three spellings of the integer 1. A writer that keeps the spelling of a number hashes the same value to different hashes. Integer-valued numbers have one canonical text whatever they were written as.

One of three spellings of the integer 1. A writer that keeps the spelling of a number hashes the same value to different hashes. Integer-valued numbers have one canonical text whatever they were written as.
A writer that prints the sign of a negative zero hashes -0 and 0 differently, though they are the same number.

Keys are sorted by the byte order of their UTF-8 form at every depth, not by insertion order and not at the top level alone. The accented key sorts after every ASCII key because its first byte is 0xC3.
A writer that sorts by UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript does by default, puts U+10000 (a surrogate pair, D800 DC00) before U+FF5E. By UTF-8 bytes U+FF5E (EF BD 9E) comes first.
Sorting array elements would make two different lists hash alike.
A string is escaped with a backslash before a quote and before a backslash and with the short escapes for backspace, form feed, line feed, carriage return and tab, and with nothing else.
Every other character below U+0020 is written as \u00 and two lower-case hex digits. A writer that uses upper-case hex, or the short escape \v, hashes differently.
encoding/json and JavaScript's JSON.stringify escape some of these by default. <, >, & and the line separators U+2028 and U+2029 are written as themselves in UTF-8, as is U+007F.
A composed letter (U+00E9) and a decomposed one (e and U+0301) are different strings and hash differently. Strings are not Unicode-normalized.
A composed letter (U+00E9) and a decomposed one (e and U+0301) are different strings and hash differently. Strings are not Unicode-normalized.
A kwarg that is absent and one that is explicitly null are different kwargs. This is the absent case, whose canonical text is the empty object.
A kwarg that is absent and one that is explicitly null are different kwargs. A writer that drops nulls hashes this like the absent case.
Empty kwargs hash as the two bytes {} and nothing else: no trailing newline, no spaces.
A number that is not an integer is written in the ECMAScript number-to-string form of its nearest double.
Below 0.000001 the ECMAScript form is the shortest digits with a lower-case e and the exponent with its minus sign and no leading zeros: 1.5e-7, not 1.5e-07 and not 0.00000015.
9007199254740992 is 2^53, the largest integer accepted.
One past 2^53 cannot be told apart from 2^53 by a writer that reads numbers as doubles, so it is refused rather than hashed ambiguously.
1e30 is an integer-valued number beyond 2^53, so it is refused whatever its spelling.
A number whose nearest double is infinite is refused as not finite, before its integer size is considered.
One case with every shape together, so a writer that handles each alone but not together shows it: nested objects, arrays of objects, booleans, null, strings, and numbers.
The baseline for the next case: the same text with LF line endings.
A body written with CRLF line endings hashes as the same text with LF, so a file checked out with either ending still verifies.
A carriage return not followed by a line feed is left as it is, so this text does not hash like the LF text.
Indentation takes part in the hash. A writer that trims lines hashes this like the original.
Trailing spaces take part in the hash.
Trailing blank lines take part in the hash. A writer that trims the end hashes this like the original.
The empty body has a hash like any other text, the SHA-256 of the empty string.
